name: Llama Guard: LLM-based Input-Output Safeguard for Human-AI Conversations
problem: Content moderation at serving time requires classifying BOTH the user prompt and the model's response, and existing moderation tools were not purpose-built for the human-AI conversation setting or for taxonomy-driven classification.
mechanism: An instruction-tuned Llama2-7b safeguard MODEL, not a filter. Incorporates a SAFETY RISK TAXONOMY that categorises the risks found in prompts, and uses the SAME taxonomy to classify the model's responses (prompt classification vs response classification). Functions as a language model performing MULTI-CLASS classification and emitting binary decision scores. Because it is instruction-tuned, the taxonomy categories and output format are ADAPTABLE per use case, enabling zero-shot or few-shot prompting with different taxonomies at the input.
speedup_reported: No latency or throughput figure. The reported results are quality: strong performance on the OpenAI Moderation Evaluation dataset and ToxicChat, MATCHING OR EXCEEDING currently available content moderation tools. The serving-cost implication is structural and recorded here rather than in the paper: this is a SECOND MODEL CALL on the critical path per interaction, at 7B parameters - which is exactly the cost problem that Llama Guard 3-1B-INT4 (pap-eff-llama-guard-3-1b-int4) exists to solve, with explicit tok/s and TTFT numbers.
notes: ADOPTION: in-production - weights are open (open_weights true) and Llama Guard is deployed as a moderation model across Meta's products and widely reused elsewhere. VENUE NOTE: no peer-reviewed venue verifiable via Semantic Scholar at verification time (rate-limited) and no arXiv comment venue, so venue = arxiv-preprint with year = ArXiv v1 (Dec 2023). THE COST POINT IS RECORDED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE IT IS THE REASON THE SUCCESSOR EXISTS: an LLM-based guardrail at 7B doubles the number of model invocations per conversation, and unlike speculative decoding there is no lossless trick for it - you either shrink the guard model or accept the latency. Pair this record with pap-eff-llama-guard-3-1b-int4, which quantifies exactly this trade with a 7x smaller model and a measured TTFT, and note the taxonomy-adaptation feature as the reason an instruction-tuned guard is preferable to a fixed-classifier approach for a repo that needs to distinguish risk categories.
